sections.label: Electricity Act amendment areas
sections.summary: MTI and EMA propose updating the Electricity Act in four key areas covering supply, infrastructure protection, procedural clarity and alignment with the Gas Act.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: The Ministry of Trade and Industry (MTI) and the Energy Market Authority (EMA) are, therefore, proposing to update the Electricity Act in four key areas: first, enhancing the security, reliability and competitiveness of our electricity supplies; second, enhancing protection of critical electricity infrastructure and safety of electrical works; third, clarifying procedural and technical provisions in the Electricity Act; and fourth, aligning regulatory provisions in the Electricity Act with similar provisions in the Gas Act for consistency.

sections.label: EMA connection direction power
sections.summary: Clause 6 introduces section 20A letting EMA direct licensees to connect electrical equipment for network expansion or supply security and reliability.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: The first amendment, in clause 6 of the Bill, introduces a new section 20A, which allows EMA to direct the electricity transmission licensee and an electricity licensee to effect a connection between their respective electrical equipment, if this is necessary for network expansion in the public interest or to ensure the security and reliability of electricity supply to the public.

sections.label: Small contestable consumers reversion right
sections.summary: Clauses 5 and 15 reflect the right of small contestable consumers to revert to the regulated tariff in specified circumstances.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: The fourth proposed amendment, under clauses 5 and 15 of the Bill, amends the Electricity Act to reflect the right of small contestable consumers, that is, consumers whose average monthly electricity consumption for the preceding continuous 12-month period is less than four megawatt hours, to revert to purchasing electricity at the regulated tariff if they cannot, or do not wish to purchase electricity from electricity retailers or directly from the wholesale electricity market, or if their electricity retailer is unable to retail electricity to them for any reason.

sections.label: Offence penalties and unlicensed electrical works
sections.summary: The amendment prescribes a maximum $1 million fine and/or five years' imprisonment, and clause 22 expands enforcement to firms using unlicensed electrical workers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: The amendment further prescribes a maximum fine of $1 million and/or imprisonment of up to five years for all offences under the section, regardless of the type of electricity infrastructure involved and whether or not the damage is earthworks-related.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: The sixth amendment, in clause 22 of the Bill, amends section 82 of the Electricity Act to expand enforcement against persons carrying out electrical works without valid electrical worker licences, to include firms that provide electrical work services to consumers using workers who are not licensed electrical workers.

sections.label: Submarine cable and electricity theft offences
sections.summary: Clause 24 makes damaging submarine electricity cables an offence, and clause 25 mandates an additional fine of three times the value of electricity dishonestly consumed.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: Second, clause 24 of the Bill amends the Electricity Act to make it an offence for any person to damage any submarine electricity cable belonging to, or under the control or management of an electricity licensee.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: Similar to the Gas Act amendments, the offence will carry a maximum fine of $2 million and/or imprisonment of up to five years upon conviction.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: Third, clause 25 of the Bill amends section 87 of the Electricity Act to mandate that the Court impose an additional fine equivalent to three times the value of electricity dishonestly consumed, on conviction for dishonest consumption of electricity and meter tampering offences.

sections.label: EMA network expansion and backup power
sections.summary: The Bill empowers EMA to direct transmission network expansion for supply security, and a Member urges expediting independent island-wide electricity sources for backup power.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The Bill will empower EMA to direct the expansion of the electricity transmission network to ensure the security and reliability of supply when necessary, including for emergency situations like this.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: However, the recent blackout highlighted how centralised our operations are and the associated vulnerabilities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I urge the Ministry to consider expediting the setting up of independent sources of electricity island-wide to provide backup power for critical installations, such as water pumps, elevators, traffic and street lights.

sections.label: Extending testbeds to more areas
sections.summary: Asks whether MTI and EMA would prioritise extending these testbeds to more areas and institutions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Would MTI and EMA make it a priority to extend these testbeds to more areas and institutions?

sections.label: Microgrids and energy technologies
sections.summary: Microgrids are being studied as they allow easier integration of energy technologies, with an upcoming urban microgrid at SIT Punggol.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
sentences.text: And we are also studying various aspects of microgrids, because these can allow for easier integration of various energy technologies.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
sentences.text: So, for example, the upcoming microgrid at the Singapore Institute of Technology's campus in Punggol will be the first urban microgrid in Singapore that will integrate various types of energy technologies, including renewable sources and energy storage.

sections.label: Electricity Act wireless amendments
sections.summary: The amendments to the Electricity Act make clear this includes wireless means in addition to physical means.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
sentences.text: The amendments to the Electricity Act make clear that this includes through wireless means, in addition to physical means.

sections.label: EMA outreach to senior citizens
sections.summary: EMA works with grassroots organisations to keep seniors informed, and the OEM rollout from 1 November 2018 will be done in zones.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
sentences.text: EMA is also working closely with various grassroots organisations to ensure that senior citizens are kept informed as well, especially seniors who are not so literate or not literate.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
sentences.text: This is one of the reasons why the nationwide rollout of the OEM from 1 November 2018 will be done in zones, so that EMA and retailers can focus their resources to help consumers better understand their options before making a decision.
